example_sentences.japanese: 全部おいしかったです。
example_sentences.english: Everything was delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は全然寝ませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn't sleep at all yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: この本は全然面白くないです。
example_sentences.english: This book isn't interesting at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は全然勉強しません。
example_sentences.english: He doesn't study at all.

example_sentences.japanese: お金はゼロです。
example_sentences.english: The money is at zero.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はゼロを書きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm writing a zero.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の友達はゼロです。
example_sentences.english: I have zero friends today.

example_sentences.japanese: 象の鼻は手のように使えるそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently an elephant can use its trunk like a hand.

example_sentences.japanese: 象はとても重いので、この橋を渡ることができません。
example_sentences.english: The elephant is far too heavy to cross this bridge.

example_sentences.japanese: 象が水を飲むところを、息子と一緒に見ました。
example_sentences.english: My son and I watched an elephant drinking water.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と遊んだら、ズボンが泥で汚くなった。
example_sentences.english: I played with the dog, and my trousers got all muddy.

example_sentences.japanese: このズボンは長すぎるので、短くしてもらった。
example_sentences.english: These trousers were too long, so I had them shortened.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車に乗るときは、ズボンのほうが便利です。
example_sentences.english: Trousers are more practical when you ride a bike.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分だけお菓子を二つ取るのはずるいよ。
example_sentences.english: It's not fair to take two sweets just for yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: テストで友達の答えを見るのはずるいです。
example_sentences.english: Looking at a friend's answers during a test is cheating.

example_sentences.japanese: あの猫はずるいから、よく犬の席に座ります。
example_sentences.english: That cat is sly, so it often sits in the dog's spot.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は注射が嫌いで、病院で泣いてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My kid hates shots and ended up crying at the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 注射は思ったより痛くなかったです。
example_sentences.english: The shot hurt less than I expected.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫に注射をするのは本当に大変です。
example_sentences.english: Giving a cat a shot is a real struggle.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は来週、目の手術をすることになった。
example_sentences.english: It's been decided that my grandfather will have eye surgery next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術の前の日は、何も食べてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You can't eat anything the day before surgery.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術が終わるまで、母は静かに待っていました。
example_sentences.english: My mother waited quietly until the surgery was over.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は自転車から落ちて、一週間入院した。
example_sentences.english: My little brother fell off his bike and spent a week in the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 入院している間、毎日、本を読んでいました。
example_sentences.english: While I was in the hospital, I read books every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 入院するなら、何を持って行けばいいですか。
example_sentences.english: If I'm going into the hospital, what should I bring?

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人は明日退院するそうです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently the person in the next bed is leaving the hospital tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 退院した日に、ラーメンを食べに行った。
example_sentences.english: The day I got out of the hospital, I went out for ramen.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が退院する前に、部屋を掃除しておきます。
example_sentences.english: I'll clean the room before my husband comes home from the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の健康診断は毎年四月にあります。
example_sentences.english: The company health checkup is every April.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康診断で、体重が増えたのが分かった。
example_sentences.english: My checkup showed that I'd put on weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康診断の結果が悪くて、兄はお酒を減らした。
example_sentences.english: My older brother's checkup results were bad, so he cut back on drinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 水と一緒に、この薬を飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please take this medicine with water.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は咳が止まらないので、毎晩薬を飲んでいる。
example_sentences.english: My older sister can't stop coughing, so she takes medicine every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 苦い薬を飲んだ後で、チョコレートを食べた。
example_sentences.english: After taking the bitter medicine, I ate some chocolate.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の怪我は軽いので、明日から学校に行けます。
example_sentences.english: My little brother's injury is minor, so he can go back to school tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 足の怪我が治るまで、走ってはいけないと医者に言われました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor told me not to run until my leg injury heals.

example_sentences.japanese: 「怪我はありませんか」と駅員が聞きました。
example_sentences.english: "Are you hurt?" the station attendant asked.

example_sentences.japanese: 階段から落ちて、手を怪我しました。
example_sentences.english: I fell down the stairs and hurt my hand.

example_sentences.japanese: ナイフで野菜を切るときは、怪我しやすいです。
example_sentences.english: It's easy to hurt yourself when you're cutting vegetables with a knife.

example_sentences.japanese: 庭で怪我している鳥を見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I found an injured bird in the garden.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、古い怪我が痛むんです。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, my old injury aches.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は朝起きると、首が少し痛むそうです。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather says his neck aches a little when he gets up in the morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷たいジュースを飲みすぎて、お腹が痛みます。
example_sentences.english: I drank too much cold juice, and now my stomach hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は目が悪いので、夜は運転しません。
example_sentences.english: My father has poor eyesight, so he doesn't drive at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 暗い所で本を読むと、目が悪くなりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you read in the dark, your eyesight will get worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 目が悪いのに、眼鏡を家に忘れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My eyes are bad, and I still went and left my glasses at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は耳が遠いので、電話より手紙のほうが好きです。
example_sentences.english: My uncle is hard of hearing, so he prefers letters to phone calls.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は耳が遠くなってから、声が大きくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my mother started losing her hearing, her voice has gotten louder.

example_sentences.japanese: 耳が遠いはずの彼が、私たちの話を全部聞いていました。
example_sentences.english: He's supposed to be hard of hearing, but he heard every word we said.

example_sentences.japanese: スポーツマンになりたくて、毎朝公園を走っています。
example_sentences.english: I want to be an athlete, so I run in the park every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は自分をスポーツマンだと言いますが、エレベーターしか使いません。
example_sentences.english: My older brother calls himself an athlete, but he only ever takes the elevator.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名なスポーツマンに会えて、息子はとても喜んでいました。
example_sentences.english: My son was thrilled to get to meet a famous athlete.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は八十歳ですが、毎朝庭で運動しています。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather is eighty, but he exercises in the garden every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動しすぎて、次の日は階段を上がるのが大変でした。
example_sentences.english: I overdid the exercise, and the next day even climbing the stairs was a struggle.

example_sentences.japanese: 体重を減らすために、夕方は一時間運動することにしました。
example_sentences.english: To lose weight, I've decided to exercise for an hour every evening.

example_sentences.japanese: 父と兄はテレビで野球を見ながら、晩ご飯を食べています。
example_sentences.english: Dad and my older brother are eating dinner while watching baseball on TV.

example_sentences.japanese: 校庭で野球をしていた男の子たちが、窓を壊してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The boys playing baseball in the schoolyard ended up breaking a window.

example_sentences.japanese: 野球は九人でするスポーツです。
example_sentences.english: Baseball is a sport played by nine people.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日にサッカーをすると、服が泥で汚くなります。
example_sentences.english: If you play soccer on a rainy day, your clothes get filthy with mud.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の友達は、野球よりサッカーのほうが好きだと言っていました。
example_sentences.english: My friend from abroad said they like soccer more than baseball.

example_sentences.japanese: サッカーを見ているとき、祖母はいつも一番大きい声を出します。
example_sentences.english: When we watch soccer, my grandmother is always the loudest one.

example_sentences.japanese: 身長が低くても、バスケットボールは上手になれますよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you're short, you can still get good at basketball.

example_sentences.japanese: 体育の授業でバスケットボールをしたので、足が痛いです。
example_sentences.english: We played basketball in PE class, so my legs hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、会社の仲間とバスケットボールをすることになりました。
example_sentences.english: It's been arranged that I'll play basketball with some coworkers this weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: テニスって、思ったより難しいですね。
example_sentences.english: Tennis is harder than I thought, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 暑すぎて、テニスをしている間に水を三本も飲みました。
example_sentences.english: It was so hot that I drank three whole bottles of water while playing tennis.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は六十歳からテニスを習い始めました。
example_sentences.english: My aunt started taking tennis lessons at sixty.

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日になると、夫はいつもゴルフに出かけます。
example_sentences.english: When Sunday comes around, my husband always heads out to play golf.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴルフをするために、朝四時に起きる人もいます。
example_sentences.english: Some people get up at four in the morning just to play golf.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はお客さんとゴルフをするのも仕事だと言っています。
example_sentences.english: He says playing golf with clients is part of his job too.

example_sentences.japanese: 水泳は体にとてもいいと、医者に言われました。
example_sentences.english: The doctor told me swimming is really good for my body.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は顔を水に入れるのが怖くて、水泳の授業が嫌いです。
example_sentences.english: My son is scared to put his face in the water, so he hates swimming class.

example_sentences.japanese: 水泳を始めてから、だんだん体が強くなってきました。
example_sentences.english: Since I took up swimming, my body has been getting stronger little by little.

example_sentences.japanese: スキーに行くなら、暖かい手袋を持って行ったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: If you're going skiing, you'd better take warm gloves.

example_sentences.japanese: スキーの最初の日は、立っているより座っている時間が長かったです。
example_sentences.english: On my first day of skiing, I spent more time sitting than standing.

example_sentences.japanese: この山は雪が多いので、冬はスキーをする人で賑やかになります。
example_sentences.english: This mountain gets lots of snow, so in winter it's busy with skiers.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は毎週、部屋で新しいダンスを練習しています。
example_sentences.english: Every week my older sister practices a new dance in her room.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のダンスを見て、妹は笑いすぎて泣いていました。
example_sentences.english: My little sister watched me dance and laughed so hard she cried.

example_sentences.japanese: このダンスは簡単なので、子供でもすぐ覚えられます。
example_sentences.english: This dance is simple, so even kids can pick it up right away.

example_sentences.japanese: この店には、外国の古い楽器がたくさん並べてあります。
example_sentences.english: This shop has lots of old instruments from abroad lined up on display.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽器は高いので、学校のものを借りて練習しています。
example_sentences.english: Instruments are expensive, so I borrow one from school to practice on.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽器ができる人が羨ましいです。
example_sentences.english: I envy people who can play an instrument.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は五歳のときから、先生にピアノを習っています。
example_sentences.english: My daughter has been taking piano lessons from a teacher since she was five.

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノは重いので、三階まで運ぶのに四人かかりました。
example_sentences.english: The piano was so heavy it took four people to carry it up to the third floor.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の家から、毎晩下手なピアノが聞こえてきます。
example_sentences.english: Every night I hear clumsy piano playing from the house next door.

example_sentences.japanese: ギターを持って、公園で歌っている青年がいました。
example_sentences.english: There was a young man in the park, singing with a guitar.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜は静かにしなければならないので、ギターは昼だけにしてください。
example_sentences.english: We have to keep quiet at night, so please only play the guitar during the day.

example_sentences.japanese: このギターは軽いので、子供にも使いやすいです。
example_sentences.english: This guitar is light, so it's easy even for kids to use.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の将来の夢は、毎年変わります。
example_sentences.english: My little brother's dream for the future changes every year.

example_sentences.japanese: 親に将来の夢を聞かれて、何も答えられませんでした。
example_sentences.english: When my parents asked about my dream for the future, I couldn't answer at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 将来の夢のために、今は英語を勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm studying English now for the sake of my future dream.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車に乗っている間が、私の読書の時間です。
example_sentences.english: My reading time is while I'm riding the train.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父の部屋には、読書のための眼鏡が三つもあります。
example_sentences.english: My uncle has three whole pairs of reading glasses in his room.

example_sentences.japanese: 涼しい秋の夜は、読書にいいですね。
example_sentences.english: Cool autumn nights are good for reading, aren't they?

example_sentences.japanese: この小説は長すぎて、まだ半分しか読んでいません。
example_sentences.english: This novel is so long that I've only read half of it so far.

example_sentences.japanese: 母が若いときに書いた小説を、引き出しの中で見つけました。
example_sentences.english: I found a novel my mother wrote when she was young in a drawer.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説の最後が悲しくて、喫茶店で泣いてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: The ending of the novel was so sad that I cried in a coffee shop.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は漫画を読みながら晩ご飯を食べて、母に叱られました。
example_sentences.english: My little brother got told off by Mom for reading manga while eating dinner.

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画は絵が多いので、漢字が読めなくても分かりやすいです。
example_sentences.english: This manga has lots of pictures, so it's easy to follow even if you can't read the kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い漫画を百冊、近くの店に売りました。
example_sentences.english: I sold a hundred old manga to a shop nearby.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子はゲームをしすぎて、目が悪くなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: My son played so many games that his eyesight got worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日は、家族みんなでゲームをして過ごします。
example_sentences.english: On rainy days, the whole family spends the time playing games.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父に新しいゲームを三回説明しましたが、まだ分からないようです。
example_sentences.english: I explained the new game to Grandpa three times, but he still doesn't seem to get it.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は日曜日の朝早く、川へ釣りに行きます。
example_sentences.english: My uncle goes fishing at the river early on Sunday mornings.

example_sentences.japanese: 釣りは静かに待つ時間が長くて、僕にはつまらないです。
example_sentences.english: Fishing is mostly long stretches of waiting quietly, so I find it boring.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の湖で釣りをするときは、暖かい服を着てください。
example_sentences.english: When you go fishing on a lake in winter, wear warm clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅館の部屋で、朝まで友達とトランプをしました。
example_sentences.english: I played cards with friends in our room at the inn until morning.

example_sentences.japanese: トランプが一枚無くなって、みんなで机の下を探しました。
example_sentences.english: One card went missing, so everyone searched under the desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹はトランプが下手なのに、いつも「もう一回」と言います。
example_sentences.english: My little sister is bad at cards, yet she always says "one more time."

example_sentences.japanese: 隣のおじいさんは、天気のいい日はいつも公園で将棋をしています。
example_sentences.english: The old man next door always plays shogi in the park when the weather is nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 将棋は覚えるのは簡単ですが、上手になるのはかなり難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Shogi is easy to learn, but getting good at it is quite hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は将棋をするとき、長い時間考えてから動かします。
example_sentences.english: When my older brother plays shogi, he thinks for a long time before he moves a piece.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社のコンピューターが壊れて、仕事ができませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The office computer broke down, so I couldn't get any work done.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館のコンピューターは、三十分しか使えません。
example_sentences.english: You can only use the library computers for thirty minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は八十歳で、コンピューターを習い始めました。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother started learning to use a computer at eighty.

example_sentences.japanese: 山の上のホテルは、インターネットが使えなくて不便でした。
example_sentences.english: The hotel up on the mountain had no internet, which was inconvenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 分からない言葉は、辞書ではなくインターネットで探します。
example_sentences.english: When I don't know a word, I look it up on the internet instead of in a dictionary.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットで買った靴が、小さすぎました。
example_sentences.english: The shoes I bought on the internet were too small.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の時間が変わったので、みんなにメールで知らせました。
example_sentences.english: The meeting time changed, so I let everyone know by email.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女からのメールを待っていて、昨日はあまり寝られませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I was waiting for an email from my girlfriend, so I barely slept last night.

example_sentences.japanese: 間違えて、姉に送るメールを先生に送ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I accidentally sent my teacher an email that was meant for my older sister.

example_sentences.japanese: このサイトは色が暗くて、読みにくいです。
example_sentences.english: This website uses dark colors, so it's hard to read.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館のサイトで、土曜日の席を予約しました。
example_sentences.english: I reserved seats for Saturday on the cinema's website.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は猫の写真のサイトを作っています。
example_sentences.english: My aunt runs a website full of cat photos.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリがあれば、電車の時間がすぐ分かります。
example_sentences.english: With this app, you can check train times right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいアプリを入れたら、携帯が遅くなりました。
example_sentences.english: After I installed a new app, my phone got slow.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語のアプリで、毎晩寝る前に漢字を十個練習しています。
example_sentences.english: Every night before bed, I practice ten kanji with a Japanese app.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんから「少し遅れる」という伝言がありました。
example_sentences.english: There was a message from Tanaka-san saying he'd be a little late.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生がいなかったので、他の先生に伝言を頼みました。
example_sentences.english: My teacher wasn't there, so I asked another teacher to pass on a message.

example_sentences.japanese: 奥さんからの伝言を、ご主人に伝えるのを忘れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to pass his wife's message on to him.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業を休むときは、朝九時までに学校に連絡してください。
example_sentences.english: If you're going to miss class, contact the school by nine in the morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布を見つけた警官が、次の日に連絡してくれました。
example_sentences.english: The police officer who found my wallet contacted me the next day.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国に住んでいる娘とは、一週間に一回連絡しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm in touch with my daughter, who lives abroad, once a week.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯を落として、画面が壊れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I dropped my phone and broke the screen.

example_sentences.japanese: 画面が明るすぎて、夜は目が痛くなります。
example_sentences.english: The screen is too bright, so my eyes hurt at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 教室の後ろの席からは、画面がよく見えません。
example_sentences.english: From the seats at the back of the classroom, you can't see the screen well.

example_sentences.japanese: このソフトを使えば、写真の色を簡単に変えられます。
example_sentences.english: With this software, you can easily change the colors in a photo.

example_sentences.japanese: 古いパソコンには、新しいソフトが入りません。
example_sentences.english: New software won't install on the old computer.

example_sentences.japanese: ソフトの使い方が複雑すぎて、店員に三回も質問しました。
example_sentences.english: The software was so complicated to use that I asked the store clerk about it three times.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年買ったデジカメを、電車の中に忘れてきました。
example_sentences.english: I left the digital camera I bought last year on the train.

example_sentences.japanese: このデジカメは軽いので、山に登るときに便利です。
example_sentences.english: This digital camera is light, so it's handy when you climb mountains.

example_sentences.japanese: デジカメの写真をパソコンに入れて、家族に見せました。
example_sentences.english: I put the photos from my digital camera on the computer and showed them to my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 金曜日の夜の番組は、子供には少し怖いです。
example_sentences.english: The Friday night program is a little scary for kids.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理の番組で見たカレーを、週末に作りました。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend, I made a curry I'd seen on a cooking show.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物の番組が始まると、うちの犬はテレビの前に座ります。
example_sentences.english: When the animal program comes on, our dog sits down in front of the TV.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝のニュースによると、今日は午後から雪が降るそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to the morning news, it's going to snow this afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震のニュースを見て、日本にいる友人に電話しました。
example_sentences.english: I saw the news about the earthquake and called a friend in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: いいニュースと悪いニュース、どちらから聞きたいですか。
example_sentences.english: Good news and bad news — which do you want to hear first?

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞の記事で、近くに新しい病院ができることを知りました。
example_sentences.english: I learned from a newspaper article that a new hospital is going up nearby.

example_sentences.japanese: 雑誌の記事を書くために、毎日ラーメンを食べ続けました。
example_sentences.english: To write a magazine article, I ate ramen every single day.

example_sentences.japanese: その記事は、名前が一つ間違っていました。
example_sentences.english: That article got one of the names wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: この小説は、英語の翻訳の方が分かりやすいです。
example_sentences.english: This novel is easier to understand in the English translation.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は会社で、外国のお客さんの書類を翻訳する仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: At his company, his job is translating documents from overseas customers.

example_sentences.japanese: アプリの翻訳が間違っていて、店の人に笑われました。
example_sentences.english: The app's translation was wrong, and the shop staff laughed at me.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越したら、市役所に新しい住所を届け出なければなりません。
example_sentences.english: When you move, you have to report your new address to city hall.

example_sentences.japanese: 市役所は駅から遠いので、バスで行ったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: City hall is far from the station, so you'd better take the bus.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は市役所の窓口で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My wife works at a service window at city hall.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は来年から大学院で歴史を勉強します。
example_sentences.english: My older sister starts studying history at graduate school next year.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院の授業は難しいけど、とても面白い。
example_sentences.english: Grad school classes are hard, but really interesting.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院に行くつもりなら、今から準備したほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: If you plan to go to grad school, you'd better start preparing now.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業したら、外国で働きたいです。
example_sentences.english: After I graduate, I want to work abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が学校を卒業したとき、家族で写真を撮った。
example_sentences.english: When our son graduated, we took a family photo.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業しても、仲間とまた会いたい。
example_sentences.english: Even after we graduate, I want to see this crew again.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は春にこの学校に入学する。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister starts at this school in spring.

example_sentences.japanese: 入学したばかりの学生は、まだ教室の場所が分からない。
example_sentences.english: Students who just started don't know where the classrooms are yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に入学するために、週末も図書館で勉強した。
example_sentences.english: I studied at the library even on weekends to get into university.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週の土曜日に漢字の試験を受けます。
example_sentences.english: I'm taking a kanji exam next Saturday.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があったので、試験を受けられなかった。
example_sentences.english: I had a fever, so I couldn't take the exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は明後日、運転の試験を受けるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Apparently he's taking his driving test the day after tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験に合格して、父がケーキを買ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: I passed the exam, and Dad bought me a cake.

example_sentences.japanese: 合格したら、すぐ祖母に電話するね。
example_sentences.english: If I pass, I'll call Grandma right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 合格するまで、何度でも頑張るつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I'll keep at it as many times as it takes until I pass.

example_sentences.japanese: 不合格だったけど、次はもっと頑張る。
example_sentences.english: I failed, but next time I'll try harder.

example_sentences.japanese: 不合格と聞いて、弟は部屋から出てこなかった。
example_sentences.english: When he heard he'd failed, my little brother wouldn't come out of his room.

example_sentences.japanese: 不合格の理由は、名前を書き忘れたことだった。
example_sentences.english: The reason I failed was that I forgot to write my name.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏の休暇に、海の近くの旅館に泊まる予定です。
example_sentences.english: For the summer vacation, I'm planning to stay at an inn near the sea.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社から一週間の休暇をもらった。
example_sentences.english: I got a week of leave from work.

example_sentences.japanese: 休暇の間、猫は隣の人に頼んだ。
example_sentences.english: While I'm on vacation, I've asked the neighbor to look after the cat.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪が降っても、彼女は自転車で出勤する。
example_sentences.english: Even when it snows, she cycles to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は八時までに出勤してください。
example_sentences.english: Please come in to work by eight tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日なのに出勤しなければならない。
example_sentences.english: I have to go in to work even though it's Sunday.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫はいつも六時に退勤します。
example_sentences.english: My husband always leaves work at six.

example_sentences.japanese: 退勤する前に、パソコンを消してください。
example_sentences.english: Please shut down your computer before you leave work.

example_sentences.japanese: 退勤してから、駅の近くでラーメンを食べた。
example_sentences.english: After leaving work, I had ramen near the station.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週は毎晩残業で、晩ご飯がいつも遅い。
example_sentences.english: I've had overtime every night this week, so dinner is always late.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は残業しないで、早く帰りたい。
example_sentences.english: Today I want to skip overtime and go home early.

example_sentences.japanese: 残業が多い会社は、あまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I'm not a fan of companies with lots of overtime.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料が上がったら、新しい冷蔵庫を買おう。
example_sentences.english: When my pay goes up, I'm getting a new fridge.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事は楽しいけど、給料が安い。
example_sentences.english: This job is fun, but the pay is low.

example_sentences.japanese: 最初の給料で、母に花を送った。
example_sentences.english: With my first paycheck, I sent my mother flowers.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社の社員は、金曜日はネクタイをしない。
example_sentences.english: Employees at this company skip the tie on Fridays.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい社員に、エレベーターの場所を教えた。
example_sentences.english: I showed the new employee where the elevator is.

example_sentences.japanese: 社員が五人しかいない小さい会社です。
example_sentences.english: It's a small company with only five employees.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長は厳しいけど、優しいところもある。
example_sentences.english: The department head is strict, but has a gentle side too.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長に書類を出すのを忘れていた。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to hand the documents in to the department head.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の間、部長は一回も話さなかった。
example_sentences.english: The department head didn't say a single word during the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の車は、驚くほど古い。
example_sentences.english: The company president's car is surprisingly old.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月、社長が工場に来るそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear the president is coming to the factory next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は三十歳で小さい会社の社長になった。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather became president of a small company at thirty.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日努力すれば、漢字も覚えられる。
example_sentences.english: If you put in effort every day, you can learn kanji too.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘はピアノが上手になるように努力している。
example_sentences.english: My daughter is working hard to get better at piano.

example_sentences.japanese: 努力したのに、結果はあまり良くなかった。
example_sentences.english: I put in the effort, but the results weren't great.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい店が成功して、町が賑やかになった。
example_sentences.english: The new shop took off, and the town got livelier.

example_sentences.japanese: 二回失敗したけど、三回目で成功した。
example_sentences.english: I failed twice, but succeeded on the third try.

example_sentences.japanese: 十分に準備したので、成功するはずだ。
example_sentences.english: We prepared thoroughly, so it should succeed.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗しても、また始めればいい。
example_sentences.english: Even if you fail, you can just start over.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理に失敗して、夜はコンビニのパンを食べた。
example_sentences.english: I ruined the cooking, so that night I ate convenience-store bread.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗するのが怖くて、手を上げなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was scared of getting it wrong, so I didn't raise my hand.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の目標は、毎朝三十分走ることだ。
example_sentences.english: This year's goal is to run thirty minutes every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 店の今月の目標は、お客さんを百人増やすことです。
example_sentences.english: The shop's goal this month is to bring in a hundred more customers.

example_sentences.japanese: 目標があると、勉強が楽しくなる。
example_sentences.english: Having a goal makes studying fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末の計画を、恋人と話し合った。
example_sentences.english: I talked over our weekend plans with my partner.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風で、旅行の計画を変えなければならなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because of the typhoon, we had to change our travel plans.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父の計画は、いつも複雑すぎる。
example_sentences.english: My uncle's plans are always far too complicated.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の説明は、とても分かりやすい。
example_sentences.english: The teacher's explanations are really easy to follow.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員の説明を聞いて、このカメラに決めた。
example_sentences.english: After hearing the clerk's explanation, I decided on this camera.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明が長すぎて、みんな寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: The explanation went on so long that everyone fell asleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先に新しい値段を説明しなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: I have to explain the new prices to our client.

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先の人とゴルフに行くのも仕事です。
example_sentences.english: Going golfing with clients is part of the job too.

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先から電話があったら、すぐ私に知らせてください。
example_sentences.english: If a client calls, let me know right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏はアイスクリームの売上が一番多いです。
example_sentences.english: Ice cream sales are highest in summer.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月の売上は先月の半分しかありません。
example_sentences.english: This month's sales are only half of last month's.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいメニューを始めてから、売上が増えました。
example_sentences.english: Sales have gone up since we started the new menu.

example_sentences.japanese: 安く売りすぎたので、利益が少しも出なかった。
example_sentences.english: We sold it too cheaply, so we made no profit at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 工場の利益が増えたので、給料が上がりました。
example_sentences.english: The factory's profits grew, so our pay went up.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の利益だけ考える人とは、仕事したくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to work with people who only think about their own profit.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い車を安く売って、十万円の損をした。
example_sentences.english: I sold my old car cheap and lost a hundred thousand yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 損をしても、約束は約束です。
example_sentences.english: Even if I lose money on it, a promise is a promise.

example_sentences.japanese: 早く買わないと損ですよ。
example_sentences.english: You'll lose out if you don't buy soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の予算は五万円までです。
example_sentences.english: The budget for the trip is up to fifty thousand yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 予算を考えると、この指輪は高すぎます。
example_sentences.english: With my budget in mind, this ring is too expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年の予算は、まだ決まっていません。
example_sentences.english: Next year's budget hasn't been decided yet.

example_sentences.japanese: タクシーに乗ったお金は、経費になりますか。
example_sentences.english: Does the money I spent on a taxi count as an expense?

example_sentences.japanese: 経費を減らすために、使わない部屋の電気を消してください。
example_sentences.english: To cut expenses, please turn off the lights in rooms we aren't using.

example_sentences.japanese: 領収書がないと、経費にできません。
example_sentences.english: Without a receipt, you can't claim it as an expense.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は新聞で経済のニュースを読むのが好きだ。
example_sentences.english: My father likes reading the economic news in the paper.

example_sentences.japanese: 円が安くなると、日本の経済はどうなりますか。
example_sentences.english: What happens to Japan's economy when the yen gets weaker?

example_sentences.japanese: 経済が悪くなって、仕事を探す若い人が増えた。
example_sentences.english: As the economy got worse, more young people started looking for work.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社とは、もう十年も取引をしています。
example_sentences.english: We've been doing business with that company for ten years now.

example_sentences.japanese: 現金だけの取引は、ちょっと怖いな。
example_sentences.english: Deals in cash only scare me a little.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国の企業との取引が決まって、社員はみんな喜んだ。
example_sentences.english: When the deal with a foreign firm was settled, the whole staff was delighted.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類提出は来週の金曜日までです。
example_sentences.english: The documents are due next Friday.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類提出の前に、部長に一度見てもらいましょう。
example_sentences.english: Before we hand in the documents, let's have the department head look them over.

example_sentences.japanese: 書類提出の窓口は二階にあります。
example_sentences.english: The counter for submitting documents is on the second floor.

example_sentences.japanese: 町の会合で、公園の掃除について話し合いました。
example_sentences.english: At the neighborhood meeting, we talked about cleaning the park.

example_sentences.japanese: 会合は七時に始まるから、急ぎましょう。
example_sentences.english: The meeting starts at seven, so let's hurry.

example_sentences.japanese: 月に一回、大学の仲間との会合があります。
example_sentences.english: Once a month I have a get-together with my university friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議には、外国のお客さんも出席します。
example_sentences.english: Some clients from overseas will also attend tomorrow's meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱があったけど、授業には出席した。
example_sentences.english: I had a fever, but I still went to class.

example_sentences.japanese: 出席する人の名前を、ここに書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write the names of everyone attending here.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は風邪で、三日も学校を欠席した。
example_sentences.english: My little brother missed three whole days of school with a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 欠席する場合は、前の日までに連絡してください。
example_sentences.english: If you'll be absent, please let us know by the day before.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは、午後の会議を欠席するそうです。
example_sentences.english: I hear Tanaka is skipping the afternoon meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が止まったので、テストに遅刻してしまった。
example_sentences.english: The train stopped, so I ended up late for the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅刻しないように、いつもより一時間早く起きた。
example_sentences.english: So I wouldn't be late, I got up an hour earlier than usual.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がかばんの中で寝ていて、遅刻しました。
example_sentences.english: My cat was asleep in my bag, so I was late.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルは、和食の朝ご飯を提供しています。
example_sentences.english: This hotel serves a Japanese-style breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震のとき、市が水と食べ物を提供します。
example_sentences.english: When there's an earthquake, the city provides water and food.

example_sentences.japanese: この喫茶店は、一人で仕事をする人に静かな席を提供している。
example_sentences.english: This café offers quiet seats to people working on their own.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄弟で協力して、重い冷蔵庫を二階に運んだ。
example_sentences.english: My brothers and I worked together to carry the heavy fridge upstairs.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族が協力してくれたので、試験に合格できました。
example_sentences.english: My family backed me up, so I was able to pass the exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 二つの会社が協力して、新しい車を作っている。
example_sentences.english: Two companies are working together to build a new car.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、ダンスの練習に参加しませんか。
example_sentences.english: Would you like to join the dance practice this weekend?

example_sentences.japanese: その料理の教室には、男の人も参加しています。
example_sentences.english: Men take part in that cooking class too.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年は忙しかったので、会社の旅行に参加しなかった。
example_sentences.english: Last year I was busy, so I sat out the company trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、野菜の値段がかなり上がった。
example_sentences.english: Vegetable prices have gone up quite a bit lately.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、元気がないね。何かあった？
example_sentences.english: You've seemed down lately. Did something happen?

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の子供は、外であまり遊ばないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently kids these days don't play outside much.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は将来、医者になりたいと言っている。
example_sentences.english: My daughter says she wants to be a doctor when she grows up.

example_sentences.japanese: 将来のことを考えると、少し不安になる。
example_sentences.english: Thinking about the future makes me a little anxious.

example_sentences.japanese: 将来は、海が見える家に住みたいです。
example_sentences.english: Someday I want to live in a house with a view of the sea.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在、エレベーターは使えません。
example_sentences.english: The elevator is currently out of service.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在の住所と電話番号を教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me your current address and phone number.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在、この市には三十万人が住んでいます。
example_sentences.english: This city currently has a population of three hundred thousand.

example_sentences.japanese: 当時、祖父は駅員として働いていた。
example_sentences.english: Back then, my grandfather worked as a station attendant.

example_sentences.japanese: 当時はまだ携帯がなかったので、よく手紙を書いた。
example_sentences.english: There were no cell phones yet back then, so we wrote a lot of letters.

example_sentences.japanese: 当時の写真を見ると、みんな若いですね。
example_sentences.english: Looking at photos from those days, everyone looks so young.

example_sentences.japanese: この町には以前、大きな映画館がありました。
example_sentences.english: There used to be a big movie theater in this town.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前より日本語が上手に話せるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: I can speak Japanese better than I used to.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は以前、銀行で働いていました。
example_sentences.english: My older sister used to work at a bank.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜十時以後は、大きい声で歌わないでください。

example_sentences.japanese: 今日からこの会社で働く田中です。よろしくお願いします。
example_sentences.english: I'm Tanaka, and I start working at this company today. I look forward to working with you.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年はありがとう。来年もよろしくね。
example_sentences.english: Thanks for this year. Let's keep it up next year too.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣に引っ越してきた人が、「よろしく」とお菓子をくれました。
example_sentences.english: The person who moved in next door gave me some sweets and said, "Nice to meet you."

example_sentences.japanese: 「このペン、借りてもいいですか」「はい、どうぞ」
example_sentences.english: "May I borrow this pen?" "Sure, go ahead."

example_sentences.japanese: エレベーターの前で、おばあさんに「どうぞ」と言いました。
example_sentences.english: At the elevator, I said "After you" to an elderly woman.

example_sentences.japanese: どうぞ、ゆっくり召し上がってください。
example_sentences.english: Please, take your time and enjoy your meal.

example_sentences.japanese: 明後日の会議は、午前でも午後でも構いません。
example_sentences.english: The meeting the day after tomorrow can be in the morning or the afternoon, either is fine.

example_sentences.japanese: その本を返すのは金曜日でも構いませんよ。
example_sentences.english: It's fine if you return that book on Friday.

example_sentences.japanese: 濡れても構いませんから、早く行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind getting wet, so let's just go.

example_sentences.japanese: 「荷物、持ちましょうか」「大丈夫です。軽いですから」
example_sentences.english: "Shall I carry your bag?" "I'm fine, it's light."

example_sentences.japanese: 傘がなくても、駅まで近いので大丈夫です。
example_sentences.english: I don't need an umbrella; the station is close, so it's no problem.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱は下がりました。月曜日から会社に行っても大丈夫ですか。
example_sentences.english: My fever has gone down. Is it okay for me to go back to work from Monday?

example_sentences.japanese: 早速ですが、今日の予定を説明します。
example_sentences.english: Getting right to it, I'll explain today's schedule.

example_sentences.japanese: 早速ですが、この書類に名前を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Let's get straight to it: please write your name on this form.

example_sentences.japanese: 早速ですが、値段について質問があります。
example_sentences.english: To get right to the point, I have a question about the price.

example_sentences.japanese: お気に召すサイズがなかったら、言ってください。
example_sentences.english: If we don't have a size you like, please let us know.

example_sentences.japanese: どうぞ、お気に召す物を一つ選んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please, choose any one item you like.

example_sentences.japanese: この和食は、お客さんのお気に召すと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think our guest will be pleased with this Japanese meal.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅から旅館まで、歩くとかなり遠いです。
example_sentences.english: It's quite a long way from the station to the inn on foot.

example_sentences.japanese: 一年でかなり日本語が上手になりましたね。
example_sentences.english: Your Japanese has gotten a lot better in a year.

example_sentences.japanese: このカレーはかなり辛いので、牛乳を飲みながら食べました。
example_sentences.english: This curry was pretty spicy, so I ate it while drinking milk.

example_sentences.japanese: 十分な時間がなかったので、最後の問題はできませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I didn't have enough time, so I couldn't do the last question.

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫の中には、四人に十分な食べ物があります。
example_sentences.english: There's enough food in the fridge for four people.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫に十分な水をあげてから、出かけました。
example_sentences.english: I gave the cat plenty of water before heading out.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は普通、朝ご飯を食べないで会社へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: My older brother usually goes to work without eating breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱が下がったので、もう普通に歩くことができます。
example_sentences.english: My fever has gone down, so I can walk normally again.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では、普通は靴を脱いで家に入ります。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, people usually take off their shoes before going into a house.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋には、一般の人は入ることができません。
example_sentences.english: Members of the general public can't enter this room.

example_sentences.japanese: 一般に、冬は野菜の値段が高くなります。
example_sentences.english: In general, vegetable prices go up in winter.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議には、一般の社員も出席できます。
example_sentences.english: Regular employees can attend tomorrow's meeting too.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は特別な日なので、レストランで食事します。
example_sentences.english: Today is a special day, so we're eating at a restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: このお茶は、特別なお客さんにだけ出します。
example_sentences.english: We only serve this tea to special guests.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員さんが特別に安くしてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The shop clerk gave me a special discount.

example_sentences.japanese: この書類はとても重要なので、無くさないでください。
example_sentences.english: This document is very important, so please don't lose it.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長は重要な会議の前に、いつも水を飲みます。
example_sentences.english: The department head always drinks water before an important meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験に合格するために、何が一番重要ですか。
example_sentences.english: What matters most for passing the exam?

example_sentences.japanese: これは叔母にもらった大切な指輪です。
example_sentences.english: This is a precious ring my aunt gave me.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館の本は大切に使ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please take good care of library books.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康は、お金より大切だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think health is more important than money.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに修理するのは可能ですか。
example_sentences.english: Is it possible to repair it by tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットで予約することも可能です。
example_sentences.english: You can also make a reservation online.

example_sentences.japanese: 可能なら、来週の月曜日に会いませんか。
example_sentences.english: If possible, shall we meet next Monday?

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間で全部の漢字を覚えるのは不可能です。
example_sentences.english: Memorizing all the kanji in one week is impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: この雪では、山に登るのは不可能だ。
example_sentences.english: In this snow, climbing the mountain is impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者は不可能だと言ったが、祖母はまた歩くことができた。
example_sentences.english: The doctor said it was impossible, but my grandmother managed to walk again.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜、大きい声で歌うのは、隣の人に迷惑です。
example_sentences.english: Singing loudly at night is a nuisance to the neighbors.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅刻して、会社の人に迷惑をかけてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I was late and ended up causing trouble for people at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫が庭で寝ていても、私は全然迷惑じゃありません。
example_sentences.english: Even if the cat sleeps in my yard, it doesn't bother me at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族の幸福を祈っています。
example_sentences.english: I'm praying for my family's happiness.

example_sentences.japanese: お金がたくさんある人が、いつも幸福なわけではありません。
example_sentences.english: People with lots of money aren't always happy.

example_sentences.japanese: その夫婦は、海の近くの家で幸福に過ごしました。
example_sentences.english: The couple lived happily in a house near the sea.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い日に熱いラーメンを食べると、幸せな気分になります。
example_sentences.english: Eating hot ramen on a cold day puts me in a happy mood.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬と公園を散歩する時間が一番幸せです。
example_sentences.english: Walking the dog in the park is when I'm happiest.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚おめでとう。幸せになってください。
example_sentences.english: Congratulations on your wedding. I hope you'll be happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年は病気や怪我で、不幸な一年でした。
example_sentences.english: Last year was an unlucky year, with illness and injuries.

example_sentences.japanese: 不幸にも、旅行の日に台風が来ました。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, a typhoon hit on the day of our trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の不幸を聞いて、とても悲しくなった。
example_sentences.english: I felt very sad when I heard about my friend's misfortune.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で旅行するのは気楽です。
example_sentences.english: Traveling alone is easygoing.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験が終わって、気楽な週末を過ごしています。
example_sentences.english: Exams are over, and I'm having a relaxed weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は最初の授業ですから、気楽に質問してください。
example_sentences.english: It's only the first class today, so feel free to ask questions.

example_sentences.japanese: あの男の人と女の人は、どんな関係ですか。
example_sentences.english: What's the relationship between that man and that woman?

example_sentences.japanese: 天気と気分には、深い関係があるそうです。
example_sentences.english: They say the weather and your mood are closely connected.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は仕事の関係で、毎月外国へ行きます。
example_sentences.english: My father goes abroad every month because of his work.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は虫に興味があって、庭でいつも探しています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother is into bugs and is always hunting for them in the yard.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の歴史に興味を持つようになりました。
example_sentences.english: I've become interested in Japanese history.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はゲームには全然興味がないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Apparently she has no interest in games at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 希望の日と時間をメールで教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please email us the date and time you'd prefer.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人からの手紙を読んで、少し希望を持つことができた。
example_sentences.english: Reading the letter from my partner gave me a little hope.

example_sentences.japanese: 将来の希望は、外国で働くことです。
example_sentences.english: My hope for the future is to work abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 目的の駅で降りるのを忘れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to get off at the station I was heading for.

example_sentences.japanese: この会議の目的は、新しい計画を決めることです。
example_sentences.english: The purpose of this meeting is to decide on a new plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 目的を決めないで、町を歩くのも楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Wandering around town with no set purpose is fun too.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字を覚えるいい方法を先生に聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked my teacher for a good way to memorize kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンが壊れたので、直す方法をインターネットで探した。
example_sentences.english: My computer broke, so I looked online for a way to fix it.

example_sentences.japanese: 他に方法がないなら、タクシーで行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: If there's no other way, let's take a taxi.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事の条件は、英語が話せることです。
example_sentences.english: The requirement for this job is being able to speak English.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋を借りる前に、条件をよく読んでください。
example_sentences.english: Read the conditions carefully before you rent the room.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜九時までに帰る条件で、出かけてもいいと言われた。
example_sentences.english: I was told I could go out on the condition that I'm home by nine.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議で私の提案が選ばれました。
example_sentences.english: My proposal was chosen at the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹から、夏にみんなで海へ行く提案がありました。
example_sentences.english: My younger sister suggested we all go to the beach this summer.

example_sentences.japanese: その提案には、少し問題があると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think there's a bit of a problem with that proposal.

example_sentences.japanese: この機械に千円を入れると、切符が出ます。
example_sentences.english: Put a thousand yen into this machine and a ticket comes out.

example_sentences.japanese: 工場の機械が止まって、仕事ができなかった。
example_sentences.english: The factory machines stopped, so we couldn't work.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は古い機械を直すのが得意です。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather is good at fixing old machines.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人と英語で話す機会があまりありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't get many chances to speak English with people from abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長に自分の計画を説明する機会をもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I got the chance to explain my own plan to the company president.

example_sentences.japanese: こんないい機会はもう来ないかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: A chance this good might never come again.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の場合は、公園ではなく図書館で会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: If it rains, let's meet at the library instead of the park.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱が下がらない場合は、すぐ病院に行ってください。
example_sentences.english: If your fever doesn't go down, go to the hospital right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 鍵を無くした場合、どうすればいいですか。
example_sentences.english: What should I do if I lose my key?

example_sentences.japanese: 家族の事情で、来月引っ越すことになりました。
example_sentences.english: Because of family circumstances, I'll be moving next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 事情を話すと、店員さんは切符を取り替えてくれた。
example_sentences.english: When I explained the situation, the clerk swapped my ticket.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が遅れた事情は、まだ誰も知らない。
example_sentences.english: Nobody knows yet what made him late.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は感情がすぐ顔に出る。
example_sentences.english: My little brother's feelings show on his face right away.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒っても、お客さんの前では感情を見せないでください。
example_sentences.english: Even if you're angry, please don't show your emotions in front of customers.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫にも感情があると思いますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you think cats have emotions too?

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は厳しい性格だけど、動物には優しい。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather has a strict personality, but he's gentle with animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉の性格なら、きっと最後まで頑張るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Knowing my sister's personality, she'll surely keep at it to the end.

example_sentences.japanese: 性格は簡単には直せないものだ。
example_sentences.english: Your personality isn't something you can fix easily.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅員の態度がとても丁寧でした。
example_sentences.english: The station attendant's manner was very polite.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の前で、そんな態度を取ってはいけないよ。
example_sentences.english: You mustn't act like that in front of the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は彼女ができてから、態度が変わった。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my son got a girlfriend, his attitude has changed.

example_sentences.japanese: この工場では新しい技術を使っています。
example_sentences.english: This factory uses new technology.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父は寿司を作る技術がすごい。
example_sentences.english: My uncle's skill at making sushi is amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 技術があれば、どこでも働けますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you have skills, you can work anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者になるのが娘の夢です。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a scientist is my daughter's dream.

example_sentences.japanese: その科学者は、毎晩星空を見ながら考える。
example_sentences.english: Every night, that scientist thinks things over while looking at the starry sky.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名な科学者でも、失敗することはある。
example_sentences.english: Even famous scientists fail sometimes.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話は世界を変えた発明です。
example_sentences.english: The telephone is an invention that changed the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄の発明は、五分で壊れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My older brother's invention broke in five minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: この発明で、たくさんの人が助かりました。
example_sentences.english: This invention has helped a lot of people.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院で日本の歴史を研究しています。
example_sentences.english: I'm researching Japanese history in graduate school.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の家のおじいさんは、二十年も蚊の研究を続けている。
example_sentences.english: The old man next door has been researching mosquitoes for twenty years.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究の結果が出るまで、まだ時間がかかる。
example_sentences.english: It will still take a while before the research results come out.

example_sentences.japanese: 実験が成功して、みんな喜んだ。
example_sentences.english: The experiment worked, and everyone was delighted.

example_sentences.japanese: 危ないので、実験のときは眼鏡をかけてください。
example_sentences.english: It's dangerous, so please wear glasses during the experiment.

example_sentences.japanese: 台所で卵の実験をしたら、母に叱られた。
example_sentences.english: I did an experiment with eggs in the kitchen and got scolded by my mom.

example_sentences.japanese: 市役所が、川の水について調査をしています。
example_sentences.english: The city office is carrying out a survey of the river water.

example_sentences.japanese: 調査によると、若い人はほとんど新聞を読まないそうだ。
example_sentences.english: According to a survey, young people hardly read newspapers.

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家が、地震の原因を調査している。
example_sentences.english: Experts are investigating the cause of the earthquake.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長に、取引先との話を報告した。
example_sentences.english: I reported my talk with the client to the department manager.

example_sentences.japanese: 報告は短くていいので、早く出してください。
example_sentences.english: The report can be short, so please hand it in soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は、犬がケーキを食べたことを父に報告した。
example_sentences.english: My little sister reported to Dad that the dog had eaten the cake.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議室は三階のエレベーターの隣です。
example_sentences.english: The meeting room is on the third floor, next to the elevator.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝、会議室を予約しておきます。
example_sentences.english: I'll book the meeting room for tomorrow morning ahead of time.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰もいない会議室から、声が聞こえる。
example_sentences.english: I can hear a voice coming from the empty meeting room.

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの受付で、部屋番号を聞きました。
example_sentences.english: I asked for my room number at the hotel reception desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 受付の人が、地図を書いてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The person at reception drew me a map.

example_sentences.japanese: 受付の机の上で、鳥が寝ている。
example_sentences.english: A bird is asleep on top of the reception desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 空港の案内を見て、出口を探した。
example_sentences.english: I looked at the airport signs to find the exit.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の案内のメールが、まだ届きません。
example_sentences.english: The email with the trip information still hasn't arrived.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母の案内で、森の中を歩いた。
example_sentences.english: With my grandmother as our guide, we walked through the forest.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、外国から来た友人に町を案内しました。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend, I showed a friend from abroad around town.

example_sentences.japanese: 入ったばかりの社員に、会社の中を案内してあげて。
example_sentences.english: Show the new employee around the office, would you?

example_sentences.japanese: 狐が僕を山の上まで案内してくれた。
example_sentences.english: A fox led me all the way to the top of the mountain.

example_sentences.japanese: 車に注意して道を渡ってください。
example_sentences.english: Watch out for cars when you cross the street.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館で電話していたら、知らない人に注意された。
example_sentences.english: I was on the phone in the movie theater, and a stranger told me off.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫は健康に注意して、毎朝走っている。
example_sentences.english: My husband takes care of his health and runs every morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 体重を毎日ノートに記録しています。
example_sentences.english: I record my weight in a notebook every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の会議の記録は、どこにありますか。
example_sentences.english: Where are the notes from yesterday's meeting?

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんの笑った顔を、カメラで記録しました。
example_sentences.english: I captured the baby's smiling face with the camera.

example_sentences.japanese: この番組は、毎週土曜日の夜に放送されます。
example_sentences.english: This show is broadcast every Saturday night.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅で、電車が遅れるという放送があった。
example_sentences.english: There was an announcement at the station that the train would be late.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風のニュースが、ラジオで放送された。
example_sentences.english: News of the typhoon was broadcast on the radio.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料は毎月この口座に入ります。
example_sentences.english: My salary goes into this account every month.

example_sentences.japanese: 銀行の窓口で娘の口座を作りました。
example_sentences.english: I opened an account for my daughter at the bank counter.

example_sentences.japanese: 口座の番号を忘れてしまって、アプリが使えません。
example_sentences.english: I forgot my account number, so I can't use the app.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母は自分の預金で新しい車を買いました。
example_sentences.english: My grandmother bought a new car with her own savings.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子はお菓子を買わないで、預金することにしました。
example_sentences.english: My son decided to put his money in savings instead of buying snacks.

example_sentences.japanese: 預金が少しずつ増えていくのは嬉しいです。
example_sentences.english: It feels good to watch my savings grow little by little.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は友達から借金をして、カメラを買いました。
example_sentences.english: My older brother borrowed money from a friend and bought a camera.

example_sentences.japanese: 借金があるうちは、新しい服は買わないようにしています。
example_sentences.english: While I still have debt, I try not to buy new clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: 借金を返すために、父は夜も働いています。
example_sentences.english: My father works nights too, to pay back the debt.

example_sentences.japanese: 保険があったので、手術は三万円しか払いませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Because I had insurance, I only paid 30,000 yen for the surgery.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の前に、外国でも使える保険を探しました。
example_sentences.english: Before the trip, I looked for insurance that also works abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車の保険にも入ったほうがいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You should get bicycle insurance too.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月で携帯の契約が終わります。
example_sentences.english: My phone contract ends next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は契約の書類をゆっくり読みました。
example_sentences.english: The company president read the contract papers slowly.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は二年の契約で借りています。
example_sentences.english: I'm renting this room on a two-year contract.

example_sentences.japanese: ここにお名前と署名をお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Your name and signature here, please.

example_sentences.japanese: 署名がないと、この書類は受付で返されます。
example_sentences.english: Without a signature, this document gets handed back at reception.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父の署名はとても読みにくいです。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather's signature is really hard to read.

example_sentences.japanese: はんこを家に置いてきたので、市役所で何もできませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I left my seal at home, so I couldn't do anything at city hall.

example_sentences.japanese: 引き出しの中に、はんこが三つも入っていました。
example_sentences.english: There were three seals sitting in the drawer.

example_sentences.japanese: 署名の代わりに、はんこでもいいですか。
example_sentences.english: Can I use my seal instead of a signature?

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は弁護士として、外国の企業で働いています。
example_sentences.english: My older sister works as a lawyer for a foreign company.

example_sentences.japanese: 契約について分からないことは、弁護士に聞きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's ask a lawyer about anything in the contract we don't understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁護士の話は難しい言葉ばかりでした。
example_sentences.english: The lawyer's explanation was nothing but difficult words.

example_sentences.japanese: 交番の警察官が駅までの道を教えてくれました。
example_sentences.english: The officer at the police box showed me the way to the station.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟の夢は警察官になることです。
example_sentences.english: My younger brother's dream is to become a police officer.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官が三十分も逃げた猿を追いかけていました。
example_sentences.english: A police officer spent thirty minutes chasing a runaway monkey.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防士が木の上から降りられない猫を助けました。
example_sentences.english: A firefighter rescued a cat that couldn't get down from a tree.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防士の仕事は危険ですが、とても大切です。
example_sentences.english: A firefighter's job is dangerous, but it's very important.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防士は毎朝、重い服を着て練習します。
example_sentences.english: Every morning, the firefighters train in heavy gear.

example_sentences.japanese: 週末、家族で海岸を散歩しました。
example_sentences.english: On the weekend, our family took a walk along the coast.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の後で、海岸にごみがたくさん落ちていました。
example_sentences.english: After the typhoon, there was a lot of trash lying on the shore.

example_sentences.japanese: この海岸は波が高いので、泳いではいけません。
example_sentences.english: The waves on this coast are high, so you mustn't swim here.

example_sentences.japanese: この島には店が一つしかありません。
example_sentences.english: There's only one shop on this island.

example_sentences.japanese: 船で島まで二時間かかりました。
example_sentences.english: It took two hours to get to the island by boat.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気がいい日は、ここから小さい島が見えます。
example_sentences.english: On clear days, you can see a small island from here.

example_sentences.japanese: 秋になると、野山が赤や黄色に変わります。
example_sentences.english: In autumn, the fields and hills turn red and yellow.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔父の趣味は、野山で鳥の声を聞くことです。
example_sentences.english: My uncle's hobby is listening to birdsong out in the fields and hills.

example_sentences.japanese: 町の子供たちは、野山で遊んだことがあまりありません。
example_sentences.english: Kids from town have hardly ever played out in the hills and fields.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎の夜は静かで、星がよく見えます。
example_sentences.english: Nights in the countryside are quiet, and you can see the stars clearly.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏は毎年、妻の田舎に帰ります。
example_sentences.english: Every summer, we go back to my wife's hometown in the country.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎は不便ですが、野菜がとても安くておいしいです。
example_sentences.english: The countryside is inconvenient, but the vegetables are really cheap and tasty.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界の色々な都市を旅行したいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to travel to all sorts of cities around the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい都市ほど、部屋の値段が高くなります。
example_sentences.english: The bigger the city, the more expensive rooms get.

example_sentences.japanese: この都市は地下鉄が便利なので、車は要りません。
example_sentences.english: The subway in this city is so convenient that you don't need a car.

example_sentences.japanese: 首都の名前を全部覚えるのは大変です。
example_sentences.english: Memorizing the names of all the capitals is tough.

example_sentences.japanese: 首都の朝の電車は人が多すぎて、座ることができません。
example_sentences.english: Morning trains in the capital are so packed you can't get a seat.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年、首都に引っ越すことになりました。
example_sentences.english: It's been decided that I'm moving to the capital next year.

example_sentences.japanese: この地方では、冬に雪がたくさん降ります。
example_sentences.english: In this region, it snows a lot in winter.

example_sentences.japanese: 地方によって、言葉が少し変わります。
example_sentences.english: The way people speak changes a little from region to region.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業した後で、彼女は地方の病院で医者になりました。
example_sentences.english: After graduating from university, she became a doctor at a regional hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 国家の予算はどう決まるのですか。
example_sentences.english: How does a national budget get decided?

example_sentences.japanese: 公務員は国家のために働く人です。
example_sentences.english: Civil servants are people who work for the nation.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい国家でも、自分の文化と伝統があります。
example_sentences.english: Even a small nation has its own culture and traditions.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史の授業で、古い文明について習いました。
example_sentences.english: In history class, we learned about ancient civilizations.

example_sentences.japanese: 川の近くに文明が生まれた理由は何でしょう。
example_sentences.english: Why do you think civilizations were born near rivers?

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母はアプリで晩ご飯を注文して、文明はすごいと笑いました。
example_sentences.english: My aunt ordered dinner through an app and laughed that civilization is amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい町での生活にも、だんだん慣れてきました。
example_sentences.english: I'm gradually getting used to life in the new town.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が来て以来、私たちの生活はとても賑やかになりました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since the dog arrived, our life has gotten much livelier.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日の生活の中で、一番大切な時間は朝ご飯です。
example_sentences.english: The most precious part of my daily life is breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は英語で日記を書いています。
example_sentences.english: My little brother keeps his diary in English.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い日記を読んで、少し恥ずかしくなりました。
example_sentences.english: I read my old diary and got a little embarrassed.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行の間に、日記を無くしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I lost my diary somewhere during the trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者は山の上で実験を行いました。
example_sentences.english: The scientist carried out an experiment at the top of the mountain.

example_sentences.japanese: 市役所では毎月、外国人のために日本語の授業を行っています。
example_sentences.english: Every month, the city office holds Japanese classes for foreign residents.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月、工場で安全の調査を行います。
example_sentences.english: This month we are running a safety inspection at the factory.

example_sentences.japanese: この会合への参加は自由です。
example_sentences.english: Coming to this gathering is entirely up to you.

example_sentences.japanese: 参加のお金は、受付で払ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please pay the participation fee at the reception desk.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなの参加こそが大切なんです。
example_sentences.english: What really matters is that everyone takes part.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の行事で、息子がダンスをしました。
example_sentences.english: My son danced at a school event.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬は行事が多くて、とても忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: Winter is packed with events, so I am really busy.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の行事に出席するのは、社員の義務ですか。
example_sentences.english: Is going to company functions something employees have to do?

example_sentences.japanese: 祭りの夜、町はとても賑やかでした。
example_sentences.english: On the night of the festival, the town was buzzing.

example_sentences.japanese: 祭りで踊るために、毎晩練習しています。
example_sentences.english: I am practicing every night so I can dance at the festival.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨のため、祭りは来週になりました。
example_sentences.english: Because of the rain, the festival was moved to next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 橋の上から花火がよく見えます。
example_sentences.english: You can see the fireworks really well from the bridge.

example_sentences.japanese: 花火に驚いて、犬が机の下に逃げました。
example_sentences.english: The fireworks startled the dog, and it ran under the desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園で子供と花火をしました。
example_sentences.english: I set off fireworks with my kid in the park.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人と将来計画について話し合いました。
example_sentences.english: My partner and I talked through our plans for the future.

example_sentences.japanese: 将来計画は、まだ決めていません。
example_sentences.english: I have not decided on my future plans yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 親に将来計画を説明するのは、少し不安です。
example_sentences.english: I am a bit nervous about explaining my future plans to my parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越しの荷物が多すぎて、困っています。
example_sentences.english: I have way too much stuff to move, and I do not know what to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が引っ越しを手伝ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: A friend helped me move.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越しは日曜日に決まりました。
example_sentences.english: The move is set for Sunday.

example_sentences.japanese: ごみは朝早く出してください。
example_sentences.english: Please put the trash out early in the morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 燃えるごみは月曜日です。
example_sentences.english: Burnable trash goes out on Mondays.

example_sentences.japanese: 海岸には、ごみがたくさん落ちていました。
example_sentences.english: There was a lot of trash lying on the beach.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫がごみ箱の中で寝ていました。
example_sentences.english: The cat was asleep inside the trash can.

example_sentences.japanese: ごみ箱に入れる前に、よく洗ってください。
example_sentences.english: Rinse it well before you put it in the bin.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅のごみ箱が減って、不便になりました。
example_sentences.english: The station has fewer trash cans now, which is a pain.

example_sentences.japanese: 着なくなった服は、リサイクルに出しています。
example_sentences.english: I send clothes I no longer wear off to be recycled.

example_sentences.japanese: リサイクルで、ごみを減らすことができます。
example_sentences.english: Recycling lets us cut down on trash.

example_sentences.japanese: このノートは、リサイクルの紙で作りました。
example_sentences.english: This notebook is made from recycled paper.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝コーヒーを飲むのが、私の習慣です。
example_sentences.english: Having coffee every morning is a habit of mine.

example_sentences.japanese: 地方によって、習慣が変わります。
example_sentences.english: Customs change from region to region.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前にゲームをする習慣は、体に悪いですよ。
example_sentences.english: Gaming right before bed is a habit that is bad for your body.
